data.dialog.forest_conl1_0: Look — the letter М! Мммм... You can't sing it for long!
data.dialog.forest_conl1_1: Consonant letters bump into something. М, С, Т, К, Н!
data.dialog.forest_conl2_0: Т-Т-Т! Tiger walks. К-К-К! Cat purrs!
data.dialog.forest_conl2_1: Letters Т and К are consonants. Hear how short they are!
data.dialog.forest_conl3_0: Letter Н — as in НОС (nose)! Also НЕБО, НОРА!
data.dialog.forest_conl3_1: I'm collecting letters in my backpack! Already five consonants!

data.dialog.forest_syll2_0: С + А = СА, С + О = СО! Сова (owl) is СО-ВА!
data.dialog.forest_syll2_1: I live in a burrow! Нора is НО-РА! Two syllables!
data.dialog.forest_syll3_0: The word НОРА is НО + РА. Two syllables!
data.dialog.forest_syll3_1: Excellent work! You can divide words into syllables!
data.dialog.forest_vl1_0: I found the letter А on the bark of a tree!
data.dialog.forest_vl1_1: The letter А is first in the alphabet and easy to sing: АААААА!
data.dialog.forest_vl2_0: Oh wow, letters О and У! They are vowels too!
data.dialog.forest_vl2_1: Vowel letters can be sung for a long time! О-О-О, У-У-У!
data.dialog.forest_vl3_0: Now we teach I and E!
data.dialog.forest_vl3_1: In the word АИСТ there are two vowels! Can you hear them?
data.dialog.g1e_abcl1_0: Hello! I am Polly! Letters G, H, I, J — learning more!
data.dialog.g1e_abcl1_1: G — giraffe, H — house. Let's continue!
data.dialog.g1e_abcl2_0: Letters K, L, M, N — the next in the alphabet!
data.dialog.g1e_abcl2_1: M — moon, N — night. What letter does MOON start with?
data.dialog.g1e_abcl3_0: Letters O, P, Q, R — almost half the alphabet!
data.dialog.g1e_abcl3_1: O — orange, P — parrot. Well done!
data.dialog.g1e_grtl1_1: Hello - hello! I use this word all the time! But Tali says: “Good morning is goodbye!” Is it true?
data.dialog.g1e_grtl2_0: My name is Polly! What is your name?
data.dialog.g1e_grtl2_1: My name is Tali! You can also say: I am Tali. How do we ask for a name?
data.dialog.g1e_grtl3_0: Thank you and Please are two very important polite phrases!
data.dialog.g1e_grtl3_1: Polite words are important in any language!
data.dialog.g1e_numl1_0: Numbers in English: one, two, three, four, five!
data.dialog.g1e_numl2_0: Numbers 6-10: six, seven, eight, nine, ten!
data.dialog.g1e_numl3_0: Simple examples in English! Six minus three? Three plus four?
data.dialog.g1e_numl3_1: Six minus three = three! Three plus four = seven! Excellent!
data.dialog.g1m_addl1_1: Count on your fingers or in your head. Try it!
data.dialog.g1m_addl2_0: Up to ten! How much do you need to add to 7 to get 10?
data.dialog.g1m_addl2_1: 7 + 3 = 10! I remember this secret: I look to see how much is missing to 10. But I still get confused with other numbers - can you check me?
data.dialog.g1m_addl3_1: 10 + 5 = 15! You are already counting like a pro!
data.dialog.g1m_c20l1_0: Hi! I am Leo from Number City — the gate opens if we guess a code from numbers 11–15. Can you help?
data.dialog.g1m_c20l1_1: Great! Numbers 11-20 are what you get when you add more to ten!
data.dialog.g1m_c20l2_0: Well done! Now numbers 16-20. They come in a row!
data.dialog.g1m_c20l2_1: Correct! 17 is between 16 and 18. You are already an expert!
data.dialog.g1m_c20l3_0: Comparing numbers! Which is bigger: 14 or 17?
data.dialog.g1m_c20l3_1: 17 is over 14! I remember: the further to the right on the number line, the more! Now I want to prove that I have learned. Will you check me?
data.dialog.g1m_subl1_0: Subtraction — we take away a part. 7 - 3 =?
data.dialog.g1m_subl1_1: Imagine 7 apples. 3 were eaten. How many are left?
data.dialog.g1m_subl2_1: 10 − 3 = 7! I learned special pairs! I want to show you - check if I remember them correctly?
data.dialog.g1m_subl3_1: First add, then subtract. You can do it!
data.dialog.g1r_grml1_0: Capital letter! Names and the start of a sentence are written with a capital.
data.dialog.g1r_grml1_1: Masha, Moscow, Tali — capitalized! Tali says: “So the word “cat” should also be capitalized — after all, it’s an animal’s name, right?”
data.dialog.g1r_grml2_0: Punctuation! A full stop goes at the end of a sentence, a question mark in a question.
data.dialog.g1r_grml2_1: Who is this? — question. Mum is home. — statement.
data.dialog.g1r_grml3_0: Questions WHO? and WHAT? Who is running? What is growing?
data.dialog.g1r_grml3_1: WHO — about people and animals. WHAT — about objects!
data.dialog.g1r_vowl1_0: Hello! I am Masha! Letters А, О, У are vowels!
data.dialog.g1r_vowl1_1: Vowels can be sung: А-А-А! In the word UTKA the first letter is U!
data.dialog.g1r_vowl2_0: Letters Я, Ю, Е, Ё are also vowels! They soften consonants.
data.dialog.g1r_vowl2_1: In the word ЮЛА the first letter is Ю! Remember it!
data.dialog.g1r_vowl3_0: Softness of consonants! КОН is hard, but in КОНЬ it is soft!
data.dialog.g1r_vowl3_1: The letter Ь shows softness. НОС is hard, НОЛЬ is soft!
data.dialog.g1r_wrdl1_0: Reading words! К-О-Т — КОТ. By syllables!
data.dialog.g1r_wrdl1_1: К-О-Т — КОТ! Д-О-М — ДОМ! I read words letter by letter. Sometimes I mix letters up — can you help?
data.dialog.g1r_wrdl2_0: The words СТОЛ and СТУЛ are similar. Read carefully!
data.dialog.g1r_wrdl2_1: ТРА-ВА — two syllables. КНИ-ГА — two syllables!
data.dialog.g1r_wrdl3_0: Reading sentences! Capital letter at the start, mark at the end.
data.dialog.g1r_wrdl3_1: Tali says: “CAT RUNS — that’s two sentences!” Is he right? No — one sentence needs a capital and an end mark!
data.dialog.g1w_bdyl1_0: Senses: eyes see, ears hear, nose smells!
data.dialog.g1w_bdyl1_1: Hands touch, tongue tastes. All are important!
data.dialog.g1w_bdyl2_0: Health is sport, exercise, healthy eating!
data.dialog.g1w_bdyl2_1: Fruit and vegetables are good for you. Sweets — in moderation!
data.dialog.g1w_bdyl3_0: Safety: do not talk to strangers!
data.dialog.g1w_bdyl3_1: Cross the road on green. Be careful!
data.dialog.g1w_natl1_0: Trees — oak, birch, spruce. They have a trunk and leaves!
data.dialog.g1w_natl1_1: Oak has acorns, birch has white bark, fir has needles. Help me remember!
data.dialog.g1w_natl2_0: Animals can be domestic or wild. A cow is domestic, a bear is wild!
data.dialog.g1w_natl2_1: Domestic animals live near people. Wild ones live in forests. Let’s check!
data.dialog.g1w_natl3_0: Weather can be sun, rain or snow! What to wear depends on the weather.
data.dialog.g1w_natl3_1: In rain — an umbrella, in snow — a coat. And care for nature!
data.dialog.g1w_schl1_0: Hello! I am Kesha! School supplies — pen, notebook, textbook!
data.dialog.g1w_schl1_1: At school we learn. In the classroom — desks and a board!
data.dialog.g1w_schl2_0: There are different lessons: maths, reading, PE!
data.dialog.g1w_schl2_1: We run in physical education and draw in art! Tali says: “In physical education we solve problems!” Is it true?
data.dialog.g1w_schl3_0: In PE we run, in art we draw! Which do you like more?
data.dialog.g1w_schl3_1: I like both! In PE I jump, in art I draw dinosaurs. Help me!
data.dialog.g2e_daysl1_0: Days of the week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday...
data.dialog.g2e_daysl1_1: Monday - Monday, I know that! And then... Tuesday? Wednesday? I've been confused since Thursday! Help me!
data.dialog.g2e_daysl2_0: Yesterday is the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today!
data.dialog.g2e_daysl2_1: Today is Monday. Yesterday was Sunday!
data.dialog.g2e_daysl3_0: Timetable: What day is it today?
data.dialog.g2e_daysl3_1: On Monday we have math. Weekly timetable!
data.dialog.g2e_phrl1_0: Please and Thank you are the most important words! Tali, do you know them?
data.dialog.g2e_phrl1_1: Please — пожалуйста! Thank you — спасибо! But I sometimes mix up when to say which. Help me!
data.dialog.g2e_phrl2_0: Excuse me — sorry! Sorry — I apologise!
data.dialog.g2e_phrl2_1: When you are in the way — Excuse me. When you are at fault — Sorry!
data.dialog.g2e_phrl3_0: Can I? — May I? You can't — No, you can't!
data.dialog.g2e_phrl3_1: Ask for permission: Can I go?
data.dialog.g2e_phrl3_2: No, you can't — this is MY sandwich, Tali!
data.dialog.g2e_schl1_0: Polly, I want to describe our classroom in English, but I don’t know the words! What is a desk?
data.dialog.g2e_schl1_1: Desk — парта! Chair — стул, board — доска, book — книга. Remember — I’ll help!
data.dialog.g2e_schl3_0: School phrases: May I come in? I don't understand.
data.dialog.g2e_schl3_1: I don’t understand. Or you can ask: Can you help me?
data.dialog.g2m_100l1_0: Hi! I’m eagle Archie! I can count to a hundred, but today I’m mixed up about tens — can you help me figure it out?
data.dialog.g2m_100l1_1: I’m a bit confused too! Archie, let’s ask our friend together. He definitely knows how to count by tens!
data.dialog.g2m_100l2_0: Place values: units and tens. 25 = 2 tens and 5 units!
data.dialog.g2m_100l2_1: Correct! The number 47 is 4 tens and 7 units!
data.dialog.g2m_100l3_0: Now I want to learn to compare big numbers. Tali, you have 82 shells and I have 78 feathers. Who collected more?
data.dialog.g2m_100l3_1: I think I did! But wait — let’s ask our friend to be sure. I feel a bit mixed up…
data.dialog.g2m_add2l1_0: Archie, I need help! I want to buy 20 bananas and 30 more coconuts. Is that 50 pieces? Or 23? I’m totally mixed up with the zeros!
data.dialog.g2m_add2l1_1: Hmm, it’s hard for me too! Let’s figure it out together — we have a smart friend!
data.dialog.g2m_add2l2_1: I think... 213? No, wait, I'll think differently. 28 + 2 = 30, and 3 more... I think 33? But I'm not sure - check me!
data.dialog.g2m_add2l3_0: I had 65 shells. I gave 23 to Archie as a gift. Archie says I have 48 left. I think it’s 42. Who is right?!
data.dialog.g2m_add2l3_1: I think I’m right! But let’s still check with our friend…
data.dialog.g2m_timesl1_0: Archie, I bought 4 pairs of socks (yes, dinosaurs wear socks!). How many socks is that? I think 6? No, 4+4=8? Help!
data.dialog.g2m_timesl1_1: Multiplying by 2 is doubling! Four pairs is 4 × 2. Let’s count together with our friend!
data.dialog.g2m_timesl2_0: I noticed something cool: answers when multiplying by 5 always end in 0 or 5! Is that true or did I make it up?
data.dialog.g2m_timesl2_1: Hmm, interesting! Let’s check on the tasks — maybe Tali discovered a great math secret!
data.dialog.g2m_timesl3_0: Tali, you have three pockets with 7 coins in each. How many coins in total?
data.dialog.g2m_timesl3_1: Three pockets of seven... I think that's 3 + 7 = 10? No, wait, that's multiplication! 3 × 7... Help me!
data.dialog.g2r_sentl1_0: Subject and predicate — the main sentence members!
data.dialog.g2r_sentl1_1: Almost! But what's missing is WHO is running? Subject! “The cat is running” is the real sentence. Can we help Tali figure it out?
data.dialog.g2r_sentl2_1: They clarify the main members of the sentence!
data.dialog.g2r_sentl3_0: Word connections in a sentence. Agreement!
data.dialog.g2r_sentl3_1: Hmm, there are words, but they are not connected correctly! The words in a sentence must be “friendly” with each other - consistent. Let's help Tali fix it?
data.dialog.g2r_shl1_0: Hi! I’m Masha! Tali, I want to teach you hard and soft consonants — but I get mixed up on some words. Can you help?
data.dialog.g2r_shl1_1: Sure! I honestly thought “hard” meant the letter was made of stone. Apparently not? Tell me!
data.dialog.g2r_shl2_0: Masha, I wrote «КОН» in a note. Masha laughs and says it’s wrong. What’s wrong?
data.dialog.g2r_shl2_1: Tali, you need the soft sign! Without it, «конь» turns into something else. Shall we explain?
data.dialog.g2r_shl3_0: Masha, I read the word ЛИМОН and my tongue got tied in a knot! Is Л soft or hard here?
data.dialog.g2r_shl3_1: Great question! In lemon, lion, people — Л is soft. But in ЛАМПА it’s hard. Can you feel the difference?
data.dialog.g2r_spl1_0: Noun — who? what? Table, mum, sun!
data.dialog.g2r_spl1_1: Haha! Almost! A noun is a word that names an object or being: CAT, TABLE, SKY. Let Tali help you figure it out!
data.dialog.g2r_spl2_0: Tali, a verb is an action word! БЕЖИТ, ЧИТАЕТ, СПИТ. What does the cat do?
data.dialog.g2r_spl2_1: It meows! Is that a verb? Wait — is МЯУКАНЬЕ also a verb? I’m confused…
data.dialog.g2r_spl3_0: Masha, I wrote in my essay: “Tali is a dinosaur.” Masha says that’s boring. We need to add an adjective!
data.dialog.g2r_spl3_1: Tali is a GREEN, CHEERFUL, SMART dinosaur! An adjective answers “what kind?” Shall we try together?
data.dialog.g2s_anil1_1: Hmm, Tali — you’re a dinosaur. And dinosaurs laid eggs! But I’m not sure which group you belong to. Tell us about mammals — we’ll figure it out!
data.dialog.g2s_anil2_2: Hmm… that’s a good question. Honestly, I’m a little unsure…
data.dialog.g2s_anil3_0: Archie, how many legs does a spider have? I think six — like all insects!
data.dialog.g2s_anil3_1: Hmm, wait. Is a spider really an insect? I’m not sure either. Let’s check!
data.dialog.g2s_bdyl1_0: Archie, why do people need bones? I’d rather be soft like a pillow!
data.dialog.g2s_bdyl1_1: Tali, without bones you’d melt onto the floor! Bones are support. Tell us how the skeleton works!
data.dialog.g2s_bdyl2_0: Archie, what does the heart do? I hear “boom-boom” in my chest!
data.dialog.g2s_bdyl2_1: Oh, that’s interesting! I know the heart is important, but I don’t remember exactly why. Tell us!
data.dialog.g2s_bdyl3_0: Eating well and doing sport — keys to health!
data.dialog.g2s_bdyl3_1: Tali! The body needs to be fed correctly - vegetables, fruits, protein. Cookies are not food for three days! Tell us what's healthy to eat.
data.dialog.g2s_pltl1_0: I planted a seed, but it won’t grow! Maybe I’m doing something wrong? Tell me about plants — I know nothing!
data.dialog.g2s_pltl1_1: Tali, a plant needs a root, a stem, leaves and water. I’ve seen many plants from above, but I don’t know the details. Explain to us!
data.dialog.g2s_pltl2_0: Photosynthesis — a plant breathes and feeds using sunlight!
data.dialog.g2s_pltl2_1: Leaves absorb light and make nutrients!
data.dialog.g2s_pltl3_0: Vegetables and fruit — the fruits of plants!
data.dialog.g2s_pltl3_1: Tali, no! Carrots are a vegetable and they grow underground. And an apple is a fruit that grows on a tree. Let's figure it out together!
data.dialog.g3e_dailyl1_0: Hello! Today we are talking about the daily routine.
data.dialog.g3e_dailyl1_1: Tell me what you do every day!
data.dialog.g3e_dailyl2_0: Great! Now let's talk about time.
data.dialog.g3e_dailyl2_1: “It’s seven o’clock” — 7:00. “Half past three” — 3:30. Let’s practice!
data.dialog.g3e_dailyl3_0: I always eat breakfast. I never wake up early. I sometimes do homework. Are these frequency adverbs?
data.dialog.g3e_dailyl3_1: Exactly! Always — всегда, usually — обычно, sometimes — иногда, never — никогда. Tali, you already know them!
data.dialog.g3e_foodl1_0: Food and drinks: apple, bread, milk, water!
data.dialog.g3e_foodl1_1: Juice means сок! Porridge means каша. Tali, you drink juice every morning — now you know the English words!
data.dialog.g3e_foodl2_0: I like pizza! I don’t like broccoli! These are the most important food phrases!
data.dialog.g3e_foodl2_1: Haha, Tali! And I like broccoli. Tastes differ! Do you like…? Yes, I do! No, I don’t!
data.dialog.g3e_foodl3_0: At the table: Can I have some water? Thank you!
data.dialog.g3e_tobel1_0: The verb to be: I am, you are, he/she/it is!
data.dialog.g3e_tobel1_1: Am with I, is with he/she/it, are with you/we/they!
data.dialog.g3e_tobel2_0: Negation: I am not, he is not, they are not!
data.dialog.g3e_tobel2_1: Not goes after am, is, are!
data.dialog.g3e_tobel3_0: Questions: Am I? Is he? Are you?
data.dialog.g3e_tobel3_1: Am, is, are go at the start of a question!
data.dialog.g3m_1000l1_0: I want to count how many scales the dragon in the picture has! Clearly more than a hundred… maybe a thousand?
data.dialog.g3m_1000l1_1: A thousand is a huge number! But together we’ll figure it out: 100, 200, 300… heading to a thousand!
data.dialog.g3m_1000l2_1: Tali, you're right! Let's check on the assignments - help me make sure that I also understand the rule.
data.dialog.g3m_1000l3_0: 356 and 298 - which is larger? I want to say 298 because the numbers are more interesting there... but is this the wrong approach?
data.dialog.g3m_1000l3_1: Haha! No, Tali. First look at the hundreds — 3 is greater than 2, so 356 is greater. Let’s practice!
data.dialog.g3m_divl1_0: Division is the opposite of multiplication! 6 / 2 = 3 because 2 x 3 = 6!
data.dialog.g3m_divl1_1: Tali, exactly! Division and multiplication are best friends. Let's test your idea on problems!
data.dialog.g3m_divl2_0: I want to divide 28 cookies equally among 4 plates. I think 7 each. But I’m not sure - help me check!
data.dialog.g3m_divl2_1: Tali, let's check! 4 × 7 = 28? Yes! So you're right. Division is always checked by multiplication.
data.dialog.g3m_divl3_0: If I know 7 × 6 = 42, does that mean I automatically know 42 ÷ 7 = 6 and 42 ÷ 6 = 7? One knowledge - three facts?!
data.dialog.g3m_tabl1_0: Times tables for 4 and 6! 4 x 5 = 20, 6 x 7 = 42!
data.dialog.g3m_tabl1_1: Multiplying by 4 — double and double again!
data.dialog.g3m_tabl2_0: Times tables for 7 and 8! Harder, but you can do it!
data.dialog.g3m_tabl3_0: I noticed something about the table for 9: 9x1=9, 9x2=18, 9x3=27... The sum of the digits in the answer is always 9! Is this true or did I make it up?
data.dialog.g3m_tabl3_1: The digits of any multiple of 9 always add up to 9! 9 x 5 = 45!
data.dialog.g3r_adjl1_1: Because the adjective agrees with the noun in gender! The ball is (red). The rose is (red). The apple is (red).
data.dialog.g3r_adjl2_0: Degrees of comparison: big — bigger — biggest!
data.dialog.g3r_adjl2_1: Tali, you yourself gave the perfect example! Positive - large, comparative - larger, excellent - the largest.
data.dialog.g3r_adjl3_0: ВЕСЁЛЫЙ — ГРУСТНЫЙ. БОЛЬШОЙ — МАЛЕНЬКИЙ. Those are antonyms — opposite words! Tali discovered this at five!
data.dialog.g3r_genl1_0: Masculine and feminine gender! Table — he, book — she!
data.dialog.g3r_genl1_1: The gender of a noun determines the adjective ending!
data.dialog.g3r_genl2_0: Neuter gender: window, sea, happiness — it!
data.dialog.g3r_genl2_1: Good idea! Middle - these are words ending in -o, -e: WINDOW, SEA, SUN. They respond to “it’s mine.” Let's check it out!
data.dialog.g3r_genl3_0: Gender of adjectives: big table, big book, big window!
data.dialog.g3r_genl3_1: An adjective agrees with the noun in gender!
data.dialog.g3r_verbl1_0: Verb in present tense: I read, you read!
data.dialog.g3r_verbl1_1: Endings change by person and number!
data.dialog.g3r_verbl3_0: Person of the verb: 1st (I, we), 2nd (you), 3rd (he, she, it, they)!
data.dialog.g3r_verbl3_1: I go — 1st person. He goes — 3rd person!
data.dialog.g3w_ecol1_0: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms!
data.dialog.g3w_ecol1_1: Tali, they are all connected! Trees feed squirrels, squirrels take away seeds, seeds grow into trees. Remove one link and the whole chain will collapse!
data.dialog.g3w_ecol3_0: People and nature. We are part of the ecosystem!
data.dialog.g3w_ecol3_1: Yes, Tali! Man is part of the ecosystem. And our actions affect the whole of nature - both positively and negatively.
data.dialog.g3w_geol1_0: Cardinal directions: north, south, east, west!
data.dialog.g3w_geol1_1: Tali, remember: the sun rises in the east and sets in the west. A compass will help with north and south!
data.dialog.g3w_geol2_0: Map and globe — a model of the Earth!
data.dialog.g3w_geol2_1: A globe is an exact copy of the shape of the Earth (ball). The map is like rolling out an orange with a rolling pin: it’s a little distorted, but it’s flat and comfortable!
data.dialog.g3w_geol3_0: Countries and capitals! Russia — Moscow, France — Paris!
data.dialog.g3w_geol3_1: Very cool! The capital is the main city of the country. Moscow is the capital of Russia, Paris is the capital of France, London is the capital of Great Britain. And you live in Bishkek!
data.dialog.g3w_natl1_0: The water cycle: evaporation, clouds, rain!
data.dialog.g3w_natl1_1: The water evaporated and rose into the sky! This is the first step of the water cycle. Then she will return with rain. Shall we tell Tali the whole way?
data.dialog.g3w_natl2_1: Almost! Oil and coal were formed from the remains of ancient living beings over millions of years. Tali, these are fossils in the literal sense - they need to be dug up!
data.dialog.g3w_natl3_1: Tali, this is a very important book! It contains a list of animals and plants that are in danger of extinction. Red is a danger signal.
data.dialog.g4e_past_l1_0: Spark, yesterday I climbed a mountain. How do I say that in English? “Yesterday we climb the mountain.”
data.dialog.g4e_past_l1_1: Tali, that’s the past tense — Past Simple! Regular verbs get the ending -ed. “We climbed” — that’s how!
data.dialog.g4e_past_l2_0: Spark, I wrote in my diary: “Last night I haved a strange dream.” Is that right?
data.dialog.g4e_past_l2_1: Tali, “have” is an irregular verb! It has a special past form — “had.” These verbs you learn by heart; they don’t add -ed!
data.dialog.g4e_past_l3_0: Spark, I’m writing a story about Anna: “Last Saturday, Anna meet her friends and they watch a film.” Is that right?
data.dialog.g4e_past_l3_1: Tali, two verbs — and both in the wrong form! Meet is irregular, watch is regular. Let’s fix them together — and your story will be great!
data.dialog.g4e_pres_l1_0: Hi! I’m Spark — Tali’s new friend on English Island! Tali just wrote in English: “She go to school every day.” I can tell something’s wrong — but I can’t explain why!
data.dialog.g4e_pres_l1_1: I tried my best! Isn’t “go” okay?
data.dialog.g4e_pres_l2_0: Spark, I need to say that the cat doesn’t eat fish. I wrote: “The cat not eats fish.” Is that right?
data.dialog.g4e_pres_l2_1: Tali, almost! In Present Simple, negation uses don’t or doesn’t — not just “not.” With he/she/it — doesn’t, with the others — don’t. Shall we try again?

data.dialog.g4m_cm_l1_1: Tali, let me show you a trick: multiply each place separately, from the bottom up. It’s like stacking floors of a house — one by one, and it’s not scary!
data.dialog.g4m_cm_l2_0: The dinosaur building crew lays 1 346 bricks a day. I need to order bricks for 5 days, but the numbers are so big… Digit, I’m scared I’ll mess up and order too few!

data.dialog.g4m_fr_l1_0: Digit, I have a problem! I cut a pizza for the party into 4 pieces. I ate one. How do I write how much I ate? A whole pizza — no, but zero — also no…

data.dialog.g4m_fr_l2_0: Digit, I’m cutting an apple into 4 parts. But… one piece came out bigger than the others. Is that still the fraction 1/4?
data.dialog.g4m_fr_l2_1: No, Tali! That’s the most important rule of fractions: the parts must be EQUAL. Otherwise the fraction just doesn’t work. Let’s cut it again — carefully!
data.dialog.g4m_fr_l3_0: My friend and I shared a pizza: I took 3/8, he took 5/8. He says he has more. I don’t believe it — the numbers look the same, only 3 and 5 are different!
data.dialog.g4m_fr_l3_1: Tali, you almost cracked the rule! When the denominators are the same — just look at the numerators: whoever has the bigger numerator has the bigger fraction. It’s like a contest!

data.dialog.g4s_emo_l1_0: Friendly, today my friend came to school with slumped shoulders and a quiet voice. I didn’t know what to say… Is that sadness?

data.dialog.g4s_turn_l3_1: Tali, game rules are an agreement between everyone playing. Breaking the rules is called unfair play. You don’t need to yell — calmly name the problem and suggest a fix.

data.intro.g2r_sentl1_0_b: Who? What? — subject. What does it do? — predicate!
data.intro.g2r_sentl1_1_b: Mum is cooking. Mum — subject, is cooking — predicate!
data.intro.g2r_sentl2_1_b: Without minor ones: “The cat is eating.” With them: “The fluffy cat quickly eats delicious fish.” You can feel the difference!
data.intro.g2r_sentl3_0_b: Words agree with each other in gender and number!
data.intro.g2r_sentl3_1_b: Red ball — masculine. Red rose — feminine!
data.intro.g2r_shl1_0_b: A consonant is hard if А, О, У, Ы or Э comes after it. ЛА, ЛО, ЛУ — hard! Remember: it’s about the sound, not stone.
data.intro.g2r_shl1_1_b: ЛА — hard Л, ЛИ — soft Л. The letter after the consonant changes everything!
data.intro.g2r_shl2_0_b: Конь, соль, мать — Ь at the end makes the consonant soft!
data.intro.g2r_shl2_1_b: Ь does not represent a sound. Only softness!
data.intro.g2r_shl3_0_b: Любовь, лимон, лев — Л is soft before Я, Ю, Е!
data.intro.g2r_shl3_1_b: You know hard and soft consonants!
data.intro.g2r_spl1_0_b: A noun answers who? what? Table, mum, sun!
data.intro.g2r_spl1_1_b: A noun names an object or person!
data.intro.g2r_spl2_0_b: A verb answers what does it do? Runs, reads, sleeps!
data.intro.g2r_spl2_1_b: A verb is an action. The cat meows!
data.intro.g2r_spl3_0_b: A RED ball, a BIG elephant, a CHEERFUL Tali. It answers what kind? which? what?
data.intro.g2r_spl3_1_b: Without adjectives everything is grey and dull. With them — bright and lively!
data.intro.g2s_anil1_0_b: They feed their young with milk. Dog, cat, elephant!
data.intro.g2s_anil1_1_b: Mammals are warm-blooded and have fur!
data.intro.g2s_anil2_0_b: Feathers, a beak, two wings — the main bird traits. Sparrow, eagle, penguin — all birds! (Not all birds fly.)
data.intro.g2s_anil2_1_b: Penguins and ostriches are birds, but they don’t fly. What matters is feathers and a beak — not flying.
data.intro.g2s_anil3_0_b: Fish breathe with gills and live in water. Insects have 6 legs (not 8!). A spider is not an insect — it has 8 legs.
data.intro.g2s_anil3_1_b: Pike, carp — fish. Butterfly, ant — insects!
data.intro.g2s_bdyl1_0_b: Bones are support. Muscles help us move!

data.intro.g2s_bdyl2_0_b: Heart, lungs, stomach — each organ has its own job inside the body.
data.intro.g2s_bdyl2_1_b: The heart pumps blood, lungs help us breathe, the stomach digests food.
data.intro.g2s_bdyl3_0_b: Veggies and fruit give vitamins. Meat and eggs — protein (building material). Porridge — energy. Sweets — only sometimes!
data.intro.g2s_bdyl3_1_b: Exercises, running, swimming strengthen muscles and the heart. Movement is life!
data.intro.g2s_pltl1_0_b: Root, stem, leaves, flower — parts of a plant!
data.intro.g2s_pltl1_1_b: Root is in the soil. Leaves reach towards the sun!
data.intro.g2s_pltl2_0_b: A plant absorbs light and makes nutrients!
data.intro.g2s_pltl3_0_b: Carrot is a root vegetable. Apple is a fruit. Tomato is a vegetable!
data.intro.g2s_pltl3_1_b: Vegetables grow in the soil or in beds. Fruits — on trees!
data.intro.g3e_dailyl1_0_b: Everyone has a daily routine. In English it is called daily routine.
data.intro.g3e_dailyl2_0_b: What time is it? It is … o'clock. Half past, quarter past, quarter to.
data.intro.g3e_dailyl2_1_b: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening.
data.intro.g3e_dailyl3_1_b: Usually before the main verb: I always brush my teeth.

data.intro.g3e_foodl1_1_b: I like apples. I drink water!
data.intro.g3e_foodl2_0_b: I like pizza. I don't like broccoli. I like it / I don't like it!
data.intro.g3e_foodl2_0_t: I like / I do not like!
data.intro.g3e_foodl2_1_b: Do you like...? Yes, I do. No, I do not!
data.intro.g3e_foodl3_0_b: Can I have some water? Thank you! Table manners!
data.intro.g3e_foodl3_1_b: Please. Thank you. You are welcome!

data.intro.g3e_tobel2_0_b: I am not, he is not, they are not. Not after am, is, are!

data.intro.g3e_tobel3_1_b: Are you ready? Yes, I am!

data.intro.g3m_1000l1_1_b: Ones, tens, hundreds — each digit's value depends on its place!
data.intro.g3m_1000l2_0_b: 247 = 200 + 40 + 7. Two hundreds, four tens, seven ones.

data.intro.g3m_divl3_0_b: Big numbers — use long division, step by step.

data.intro.g3m_tabl2_1_b: 8 × 8 = 64 - “eight eight sixty four.” Remember in pairs!

data.intro.g3r_adjl1_0_b: Red ball, red rose, red apple!
data.intro.g3r_adjl1_1_b: The adjective is in the same gender and number as the noun!
data.intro.g3r_adjl3_0_b: Words with opposite meanings: big — small, hot — cold.
data.intro.g3r_adjl3_1_b: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings!
data.intro.g3r_genl3_0_b: Big table, big book, big window!
data.intro.g3r_genl3_1_b: An adjective agrees with the noun!
data.intro.g3r_verbl1_0_b: I read, you read, he reads. Endings change by person!
data.intro.g3r_verbl1_1_b: 1st person: I, we. 2nd: you. 3rd: he, she, it, they!
data.intro.g3r_verbl2_0_b: Read (m.), read (f.), read (n.). Suffix -л and ending by gender!
data.intro.g3r_verbl2_1_b: I read (m.). She read (f.). It read (n.)!
data.intro.g3r_verbl3_0_b: 1st person: I go, we go. 2nd: you go. 3rd: he goes!
data.intro.g3r_verbl3_1_b: Endings change by person and number!

data.intro.g3w_ecol2_0_b: Plant — hare — wolf! Who eats what!
data.intro.g3w_ecol2_1_b: Everyone is part of the chain!
data.intro.g3w_ecol3_0_b: We are part of the ecosystem! Our actions affect nature!
